Q912416.label: 1949 Canadian federal election
Q912416.summary: The 1949 Canadian federal election was held June 27, 1949, to elect members of the House of Commons of Canada of the 21st Parliament of Canada.

Q887328.label: Salvador Castaneda Castro
Q887328.summary: Salvador Castaneda Castro was a Salvadoran military officer who served as the 28th President of El Salvador from 1 March 1945 to his overthrow on 14 December 1948. He also served as Minister of Government, Promotion, Agriculture, Labor, Sanitation, and Charity from 1931 to 1935 and as Minister of War, the Navy, and Aviation during March 1945.

Q3984928.label: Third Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q3984928.desc: To permit the state to join the European Communities
aliases: 3rd Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q3984928.wiki: Third Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q3984928.summary: The Third Amendment of the Constitution Act 1972 is an amendment to the Constitution of Ireland that permitted the State to join the European Communities, which would later become the European Union, and provided that European Community law would take precedence over the constitution. It was approved by referendum on 10 May 1972, and signed into law by the President of Ireland Éamon de Valera on 8 June of the same year.

Q32.label: Luxembourg
Q32.summary: Luxembourg, officially the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, is a landlocked country in Western Europe. It is bordered by Belgium to the west and north, Germany to the east, and France to the south and west. Its capital and most populous city, Luxembourg City, is one of the four institutional seats of the European Union and hosts several EU institutions, notably the Court of Justice of the European Union, the highest judicial authority in the EU.

Q1190944.label: 2001 Liechtenstein general election
Q1190944.summary: General elections were held in Liechtenstein between 9 and 11 February 2001 to elect the 25 members of the Landtag. The Progressive Citizens' Party (FBP) won a majority of thirteen seats, with the Patriotic Union (VU) winning eleven. The Free List (FL) won one seat. Voter turnout was 86.1%.

Q779296.label: 2006 Hungarian parliamentary election
Q779296.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Hungary on 9 April 2006, with a second round of voting in 110 of the 176 single-member constituencies on 23 April. The Hungarian Socialist Party emerged as the largest party in the National Assembly with 186 of the 386 seats, and continued the coalition government with the Alliance of Free Democrats.

Q1682464.label: Jan Černý
Q1682464.desc: Czechoslovak civil servant, prime minister, and provincial president of Moravia (1874-1959)
Q1682464.img: Černý Jan, Album representantů všech oborů veřejného života československého 1927.jpg
Q1682464.summary: Jan Černý was a Czech civil servant and politician. He was the prime minister of Czechoslovakia from 1920 to 1921 and in 1926. He also served as the provincial president (governor) of Moravia in 1918–1920, 1921–1928 and 1929–1939.

Q3511328.label: 2006 Czech Senate election
Q3511328.summary: Senate elections were held in the Czech Republic on 20 and 21 October 2006, with a second round on 27 and 28 October. The result was a victory for the Civic Democratic Party, which won 41 of the 81 seats. Voter turnout was 41% in the first round and just 21% in the second.

Q7362592.label: Romanian constitutional referendum, 1991
Q7362592.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Romania on 8 December 1991. The new constitution was approved by 79% of voters.

Q1465376.label: Communist Party of Lithuania
Q1465376.summary: The Communist Party of Lithuania is a banned Marxist-Leninist party in Lithuania. The party was established in early October 1918 and operated clandestinely until it was legalized in 1940 after the Soviets claimed the Baltics. The party was banned in August 1991, following the coup attempt in Moscow which later led to the dissolution of the Soviet Union and the end of the Lithuanian SSR. It remains illegal in modern day Lithuania and continues to operate, albeit having a negligible presence in Lithuanian politics.

Q272416.label: Salome Zourabichvili
Q272416.desc: Georgian politician and former French diplomat, fifth President of Georgia (2018–2024)
Q272416.img: President of Georgia Salome Zourabichvili in Brussels, 2019 (cropped).jpg
Q272416.summary: Salomé Nino Zourabichvili is a French-born Georgian politician and former diplomat who served as the fifth president of Georgia, becoming the first woman to be elected as president in the country's history. As a result of the constitutional amendments that came into effect in 2024, Zourabichvili became the last popularly elected president; under the new constitutional rules, Georgian presidents are to be elected indirectly by the Georgian Electoral Assembly.

Q3586592.label: 1964 Icelandic presidential election
Q3586592.summary: Presidential elections were scheduled to be held in Iceland in 1964. However, incumbent President Ásgeir Ásgeirsson was the only candidate, and the election was uncontested.

Q5152.label: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
Q5152.desc: founding father of the Republic of Turkey (c. 1881–1938)
Q5152.summary: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was a Turkish field marshal and statesman who was the founder of the Republic of Turkey and served as its first president from 1923 until his death in 1938. He led sweeping reforms, turning Turkey into an industrialising nation. Ideologically a republican, secularist, and nationalist, his policies and socio-political theories became known as Kemalism. Atatürk's personality cult and the Kemalist historiography developed around it have had significant and ongoing influences on Turkey's political culture and historical narrative.

Q3444768.label: assassination of Zoran Đinđić
Q3444768.desc: 2003 murder of the Prime Minister of Serbia
Q3444768.summary: Zoran Đinđić, the sixth Prime Minister of the Republic of Serbia, was assassinated on Wednesday 12 March 2003, in Belgrade, Serbia. Đinđić was fatally shot by a sniper while exiting his vehicle outside of the back entrance of the Serbian government headquarters.

Q6627360.label: Battle of Raqqa
Q6627360.summary: The Battle of Raqqa, also known as the First Battle of Raqqa and code named by rebels as the "Raid of the Almighty", was fought for control of the northern Syrian city of Raqqa during the Syrian civil war between Sunni Islamist rebel insurgents and the Syrian Arab Army.

Q836128.label: Battle of Bir Hakeim
Q836128.desc: 1942 part of the battle of Gazala in the Western Desert Campaign of World War II
Q836128.summary: The Battle of Bir Hakeim took place at Bir Hakeim, an oasis in the Libyan desert southwest of Tobruk, during the Battle of Gazala. The 1st Free French Brigade defended the position from 26 May to 11 June against Axis forces of the Panzerarmee Afrika that captured Tobruk ten days later.

Q2026016.label: Operation Cartwheel
Q2026016.desc: 1943 major military strategy for the Allies in the Pacific theater of World War II
Q2026016.summary: Operation Cartwheel (1943–1944) was a major military operation undertaken by the Allies in the Pacific theatre of World War II. The ultimate goal of Cartwheel was to neutralize the major Japanese base at Rabaul. The operation was directed by the Supreme Allied Commander in the South West Pacific Area (SWPA), General Douglas MacArthur, whose forces had advanced along the northeast coast of New Guinea and occupied nearby islands. US forces from the South Pacific Area, under Admiral William Halsey, advanced through the Solomon Islands toward Bougainville.

Q5307936.label: Drive on Munda Point
Q5307936.desc: battle of the New Georgia campaign during World War II
Q5307936.summary: The Drive on Munda Point was an offensive by mainly United States Army forces against Imperial Japanese forces on New Georgia in the Solomon Islands from 2–17 July 1943. The Japanese forces, mainly from the Imperial Japanese Army, were guarding an airfield at Munda Point on the western coast of the island that the U.S. wished to capture as one of the key objectives of the New Georgia campaign. After landing around Zanana on 2 July from Rendova, U.S. troops began a westward advance towards the airfield at Munda. Q700960.label: Battle of Kiev
Q700960.desc: 1943 battle, part of the Eastern Front of World War II
Q700960.summary: The Second Battle of Kiev, known on the German side as the Defensive battle in the Kiev-Zhitomir area, was a part of a much wider Soviet offensive in Ukraine known as the Battle of the Dnieper involving three strategic operations by the Soviet Red Army and its Czechoslovak units and one operational counterattack by the Wehrmacht, which took place between 4 November and 22 December 1943.

Q16864800.label: Operation Gisela
Q16864800.summary: Operation Gisela was the code name for a German military operation of the Second World War. Gisela was an intruder operation against RAF Bomber Command during the Defence of the Reich campaign. It was the last big operation launched by the Luftwaffe Nachtjagdgeschwader during the conflict.

Q16170016.label: Battle of the Imjin River
Q16170016.desc: 1951 major confrontation during the Chinese Spring Offensive of the Korean War
Q16170016.img: US 3rd infantry troops, before Imjin River patrol, Korea 17-April-1951.jpg
Q16170016.summary: The Battle of the Imjin River, also known as the Battle of Solma-ri or Battle of Gloster Hill in South Korea, or as Battle of Xuemali in China, took place 22–25 April 1951 during the Korean War. Troops from the Chinese People's Volunteer Army (PVA) attacked United Nations Command (UN) positions on the lower Imjin River in an attempt to achieve a breakthrough and recapture the South Korean capital Seoul.

Q840736.label: 2005 Nalchik raid
Q840736.desc: militant attack during the Second Chechen War in Russia
Q840736.summary: The 2005 raid on Nalchik was a raid by a large group of Islamic militants on Nalchik, in the Kabardino-Balkar Republic (KBR) of southern Russia, on 13 October 2005.

Q3079712.label: Party of the Democratic Left
Q3079712.summary: The Party of the Democratic Left was a social-democratic political party in Slovakia from 1990 to 2004. It was founded in 1990 out of the Communist Party of Slovakia.

Q26934816.label: Alliance of Liberals and Democrats Party
Q26934816.summary: The Alliance of Liberals and Democrats was a minor liberal political party in Romania which was officially absorbed in its entirety by the National Liberal Party (PNL), from which it initially seceded in 2015, during late March 2022. Throughout its relatively short political history, it was mostly associated with the Social Democratic Party (PSD) at governance, firstly between 2014 and 2015 and the once more for the last time between 2017 and 2019.

Q4128.label: Louis Aragon
Q4128.summary: Louis Aragon was a French poet who was one of the leading voices of the surrealist movement in France. He co-founded with André Breton and Philippe Soupault the surrealist review Littérature. He was also a novelist and editor, a long-time member of the Communist Party and a member of the Académie Goncourt. After 1959, he was a frequent nominee for the Nobel Prize in Literature.

Q616992.label: Governorate of Montenegro
Q616992.desc: short-lived territory on the Balkan Peninsula between 1941–1943
Q616992.summary: The Italian governorate of Montenegro existed from October 1941 to September 1943 as an occupied territory under military government of the Kingdom of Italy during World War II. Although the Italians had intended to establish a quasi-independent Montenegrin kingdom, these plans were permanently shelved after a popular uprising in July 1941. Following the Italian surrender in September 1943, the territory of Montenegro was occupied by German forces which withdrew in December 1944.
